note:
FEATURE / WORLDBUILDER / VEGETATION ISSUE: Kentridge and its surrounding playable area currently read as nearly barren. Human inspection shows grass only as isolated blades/clumps separated by very large empty distances (roughly the impression of one blade every tens of metres), and the grass does not visibly appear to animate. The desired result is grassy countryside with real meadow regions: broad contiguous areas that read as filled with grass at gameplay scale.

Use the recently added packed procedural grass presentation, not the legacy grass sprite or a new Kentridge-only renderer. The current production path includes `Assets/VoxelEngine/Rendering/Runtime/Vegetation/ProceduralGrassBatch.cs`, where semantic Grass/Nettle instances are expanded into multiple blades and the presentation is intended to support per-instance density, wind, camera-facing reconstruction, and character push. Determine why Kentridge is feeding this path so sparsely and why wind motion is not visibly reaching the built scene. If the shared shader/presentation animation is missing or broken, fix it in the reusable rendering/vegetation layer.

TOP-LEVEL WORLDBUILDER CAPABILITY: WorldBuilder must be able to author ecology/biome rules per world area rather than scenes directly placing arbitrary vegetation. Add or generalize a reusable area ecology/vegetation policy that can express at minimum: (1) which vegetation kinds are allowed in an area; (2) per-kind density/coverage or equivalent spawn intensity; (3) deterministic variation/seed behavior; (4) exclusion/clearance rules so grass does not populate roads, building footprints/interiors, water, cliffs or other invalid surfaces; and (5) the allowed ambient animal-life kinds / spawn policy for the area, even if no animals are enabled by this ticket. Scene composition should select semantic policies/parameters; it must not scatter hand-authored grass coordinates.

KENTRIDGE INITIAL ECOLOGY: For now, the vegetation allowlist for the relevant Kentridge countryside/meadow areas should contain only the new procedural grass presentation (`VegetationKind.Grass` or the canonical semantic kind that routes to it). Do not mix in the old grass sprite, nettles, flowers, shrubs, trees, or other ground vegetation merely to make the scene look busier. The ambient-animal allowlist for these areas should be empty for now; this ticket establishes the WorldBuilder policy hook so animals can be enabled intentionally later rather than appearing implicitly.

DENSITY / MEADOW REQUIREMENT: Kentridge must include at least one clearly readable, contiguous meadow region with thousands of generated grass blades. The hard minimum for closure is 3,000 blades attributable to one meadow region in the built application, with a normal gameplay camera view that reads as a filled field rather than sparse accents. Density should be controlled by the WorldBuilder area policy, not by renderer-side magic numbers or by globally increasing grass everywhere. Other Kentridge ground can use lower or zero density as appropriate, but meadow boundaries and transitions should look natural and should respect traversal/structure exclusions.

ANIMATION REQUIREMENT: Grass must visibly move over time in the exact built Kentridge application through the shared wind/animation path. A source assertion that a wind parameter exists, a shader compile, or a static screenshot is not enough. Motion must be visually observable from a fixed or near-fixed gameplay camera while the player is stationary, without requiring debug controls. If the intended shader already has wind, verify the production material/shader bindings, time input, amplitudes, batching data, and player-build shader inclusion instead of layering a second animation system on top.

ARCHITECTURE BOUNDARY: All vegetation type restrictions and density/coverage choices must come from the top-level WorldBuilder/ecology composition path. Kentridge may select an ecology profile, define meadow regions semantically, and set density/coverage parameters, but it may not spawn thousands of GameObjects, manually write thousands of vegetation coordinates, implement a Kentridge-only scatter loop, or fork the grass shader. Any missing capability belongs in reusable WorldBuilder / vegetation / ambient-life APIs.

VISUAL INSPECTION IS A MANDATORY CLOSURE GATE: This issue may not move to pending or closed based only on unit/EditMode tests, object counts, source inspection, or a crash-free scene launch. Human visual inspection of the exact built-application `KentridgePlayableSlice` is required. Durable evidence must include: (a) a normal gameplay approach view showing a meadow as dense grass-covered terrain; (b) a closer player-height view showing that the field is made of the new procedural blades and is not obviously tiled/sparse/floating; (c) a runtime count or equivalent durable diagnostic proving at least 3,000 blades belong to that meadow; and (d) two or more time-separated frames from the same stationary viewpoint (or a short captured sequence) proving blade silhouettes/poses visibly change due to animation/wind. The issue cannot be closed unless a reviewer can plainly see both dense meadow coverage and animation in the built application.

ACCEPTANCE: (1) WorldBuilder exposes reusable per-area ecology controls for allowed vegetation kinds and density/coverage, plus an ambient-animal allowlist/spawn-policy hook; (2) Kentridge config uses that top-level path and currently allows only the new procedural grass vegetation, with no ambient animal kinds enabled; (3) at least one Kentridge meadow contains >=3,000 blades and visually reads as a full meadow rather than isolated grass every tens of metres; (4) grass visibly animates in normal built gameplay while the player is stationary; (5) roads, structures, interiors, water, steep/invalid terrain and other exclusions are not carpeted incorrectly; (6) no legacy grass sprite, scene-local grass scatter implementation, thousands of grass GameObjects, or Kentridge-specific shader fork is introduced; (7) focused behavioral regressions exercise the production WorldBuilder area-policy path, allowed-kind filtering, density behavior, determinism, exclusions, and empty animal allowlist; (8) the exact built-application Kentridge harness reaches a usable rendered scene without startup/runtime exceptions; (9) durable visual evidence satisfies the mandatory meadow-density and animation checks above; and (10) blast radius plus CPU/GPU/memory/build-time cost of thousands of animated blades is measured against existing vegetation/rendering budgets before closure.
